lens_summary: Literature lens (Ultrack, linajea, Trackastra, HOCT, ELEPHANT, CELLECT, TGMM/TrackMate, ByteTrack, shift-and-stitch/DARK). In published work the big jumps come from two things. (1) Detectors trained so that unannotated voxels are NOT negatives: linajea masks the loss to annotated neighbourhoods, and PU learning / dense pseudo-labels do the same job. (2) Committing to nodes late: Ultrack selects among segmentation hypotheses with an ILP over time, and ByteTrack associates low-score detections to tracklets (+1..10 IDF1 across 9 trackers, github.com/ifzhang/ByteTrack). Retraining for (1) does not fit 4 days. Our all-199 scratch run scored 0.920, leonixis' 60-epoch all-train retrain 0.947, and moving the encoder under the frozen edge net cost -0.038 (Le, discussions_summary.md). Part (2) can ship. The public detector's loss treats every unannotated voxel as a negative (train_unet_transformer.py l.539-593: single-voxel target, neg_weight 0.1), so on unseen embryos it pushes real nuclei below 0.965. The x138 kernel already dumps every peak >= 0.3 (BIOHUB_LOWDET_THRESHOLD, experiments/ext_x138/biohub-x138.ipynb cells 0/4). Today that pool is used only by readmit (score >= 0.965 near open ends) and the gap filler (bridging end->start). Nothing extends a track through low-score peaks or starts a track from a persistent low-score chain. The FN anatomy says this is where the loss sits. Detection-side FN are 2,929 of 6,732 (a_never 1,907, a_tail 606). The swap/u/v classes (oracle +0.065) are 'annotated nucleus between two of our tracks, 9.4 um apart, matched at 4.4 um': a missing or merged node, not a link choice (edge_anatomy/l6_fn_anatomy_report.md s.3). A node-count check with the official formula on the exp02 hold12 validator rows gives 3.6-5.0% break-even precision for an added node, i.e. nodes are cheap and recall is expensive. It matches friend B's NMS result (-7.9% nodes = -0.026). Sub-voxel localisation is NOT the lever: polyphase/shift-and-stitch was refuted by 3 v2 skeptics (grid RMS 0.47 um against 4.4 um swap offsets), and I agree. HONEST CEILING: all detection-side classes together are +0.02 local (2,929 x 7.4e-6), and swap/u/v add +0.065 only if missing nodes cause them. A realistic hypothesis-selection stage captures 10-25% of that, so +0.001..+0.005 public per idea, not additive. With the x138 base (0.953 expected), the expected landing is ~0.955-0.958 and the optimistic one ~0.962. 0.99 is unreachable: it needs adj_edge ~0.95 AND div J ~0.4 on an unseen embryo, which exceeds today's LB top (0.975). What 0.99 would take is a dense-supervised detector plus hypothesis-selecting ILP, retrained jointly with the edge network. That is weeks of work and several GPU-days.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Lowering the detection threshold is closed (0.965->0.95 flat on the LB, 0.99 = -0.005, threshold 0.93-0.985 flat locally), so sub-threshold peaks carry no value.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: Every one of those tests admitted sub-threshold peaks WITHOUT temporal selection, so they fed the ILP and relink peaks that could steal or duplicate matches. Also, 0.965->0.95 adds only a sliver of peaks. The 0.99 result (-0.005) shows the opposite: peaks just above threshold are valuable. The metric says added nodes are cheap: break-even precision is 3.6-5.0% of added nodes being real (annotated-rate) nuclei. Persistence-gated admission (hysteresis/BYTE) was never tested, and x138's readmit+gapfill (a partial version) is exactly what lets the head's +0.007 work.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: The head retrain on 199 videos failed a fair kill test (embryo-held-out: new head 12% worse than the public head on 6bba->44b6).
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: The public V1284 head was trained on a 20-movie TRAIN capture drawn from BOTH embryos (~10+10). In the embryo-held-out comparison, the new head had never seen the held-out embryo while the public head had, so the comparison was in-sample for the public head only. A fair test compares both heads on movies outside the public head's 20-movie capture, with the new head trained on both embryos (leak-group folds). The leak-group OOF (-18.9% distance) is closer to that and was positive. This does not make the retrain a step change (v2 estimate +0.0003..0.002). It means the line was closed on a biased test.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Ultrack is a dead end for us (snapping to Ultrack points hurt; adding Ultrack points costs +30-40% nodes).
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: Snapping ALL nodes and adding ALL unmatched Ultrack points are both unselective operations. The same measurement shows that the missing-node classes are exactly where Ultrack-like hypotheses help. For a_never GT, an Ultrack point is at median 2.3 um (47% < 2 um) while our nearest node sits on ANOTHER Ultrack object. For swaps, GT->Ultrack is 2.4 um vs GT->pred 3.7 um. The literature lesson of Ultrack is SELECTION of hypotheses by temporal consistency, which was never tried. tracksdata's ILPSolver (the solver we already run) has node_weight and overlap constraints for this purpose.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: v2: 0.97 is unreachable by post-processing alone because post-processing cannot touch detection.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: Partly right on the number, wrong on the reason. Post-processing in x138 already holds detection-side information (the >= 0.3 peak dump), and x138's own +0.007 came from detection-side post-processing (readmit + gapfill + head). The v2 ceiling table summed only the kept ideas and had no item for the detection-side FN classes (43.5% of FN). I still think 0.97 is out of reach by 29 Sep. But the missing-node lever is the one remaining class with a ceiling above +0.01, and it is reachable from the lowdet pool.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Sub-voxel localisation (polyphase / DARK) remains an open lever after x138 showed positions matter.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: I agree with the v2 refutation and do not re-open it. The swap offsets (4.4 um) are an order of magnitude above grid noise (0.47 um RMS), and the measured dose-response is +0.001-0.002. The x138 head's gain mixes bias correction, float z and trilinear features, so it does not scale polyphase.

hypotheses.title: BYTE-style track extension and hysteresis births from x138's low-score peak pool
hypotheses.mechanism: The detector was trained with single-voxel positives at annotated nuclei and every other voxel as a negative (tools/repo/scripts/train_unet_transformer.py l.539-593, neg_weight 0.1). So it learned to push unannotated and hard nuclei down, and on unseen embryos real nuclei fall below the 0.965 threshold. The loss agrees. Detection-side FN are 2,929 of 6,732 (a_never 1,907, a_tail 606, linefit 354). The swap/u_diverted/v_taken classes (4,582 FN, oracle +0.065) are GT nuclei lying between two of our tracks ~9.4 um apart and matched at 4.4 um, i.e. a node missing at the right place (experiments/l2_daughternet/edge_anatomy/l6_fn_anatomy_report.md s.1, s.3). In 44b6, a_never GT has an Ultrack object at median 2.3 um while our nearest node sits on another object (research/wf_ideas_v2/r2_critic.notes.md). x138 already dumps every local maximum >= 0.3 of the fused map (BIOHUB_LOWDET_THRESHOLD=0.3) but uses it only for readmit (>= 0.965 near open ends) and the gap filler (bridging an end to a start through 0.5+ peaks). The track-level decision that ByteTrack and hysteresis thresholding make is missing: continue a track through low-score detections that sit where the motion predicts, and accept a low-score chain as a new track only if it persists. The metric makes this cheap. Per video, an added node costs 0.1*J/N_est of adjusted J, while a correct annotated node recovers up to 2 edges worth 1/D each. With E/N_est = annotation fraction, break-even precision is 3.6-5.0% on all 12 hold12 videos (computed from experiments/exp02_pub941_holdout12/results/validator_results.csv).
hypotheses.change: New stage in x138 cell 5 (post-processing), after readmit + second relink + gap filler and BEFORE the short-track filter and linefit, as a patch 'byteext' in tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 (knobs default off = byte-identical). Pool = load_low_detections() (score >= S_EXT, > GAPFILL_EXCLUDE_UM 2.0 from any node). (a) EXTENSION: for every track end at t < T-1, predict p = x_t + v_t, where v_t is the neighbourhood-flow vector the flow-prior relink already computes (or the last step). Take the highest-score free pool peak at t+1 within R_EXT = 3.5 um of p (continuation step p90 3.35 um, discussion 740573). Add node + edge, iterate up to K_EXT = 4 frames, and stop at a frame without a peak. Mirror backwards from track starts. Each peak is used once, greedy by score. If the extension reaches a track start (or end), join and stop. (b) BIRTHS (hysteresis): chain the remaining free peaks with score >= S_BIRTH by mutual-nearest-neighbour steps <= 3.5 um. Keep chains of length >= MIN_TRACK_LEN (6) with median score >= S_BIRTH_MED that stay > 4 um from existing nodes on >= 80% of frames. Guard: per video, added nodes <= 3% (like GAPFILL_MAX_ADDED_FRAC), else revert (a) then (b). Added nodes carry the integer peak coordinate (no head) and go through linefit like the others. Pre-registered primary config: S_EXT 0.5, R_EXT 3.5, K_EXT 4, S_BIRTH 0.8, S_BIRTH_MED 0.9. Arms: (a) only, (a)+(b).

hypotheses.upper_bound: Local units: 1 FN->TP = +7.4e-6 (D = 122,151+6,846+6,732 = 135,729; wf_ideas_v2 arithmetic verifier). Directly reachable classes: a_never + a_tail = 2,513 FN -> +0.0186. Of the swap/u/v oracle (+0.065), only the share caused by a missing node counts; unknown, measured in step 0. Node cost: +1% nodes = -0.1*0.914*0.01 = -0.0009, and the 3% guard caps it at -0.0027. Ceiling with every a_never/a_tail recovered and the cap used: ~+0.016 local. Realistic: 10-25% of those classes -> +0.0019..+0.0047, minus 0.0005..0.0015 node cost -> +0.001..+0.003 local. On the test embryos the detector is out-of-sample, so the pool holds more annotated nuclei than on train, and the local figure should under-state the test effect (guess).
hypotheses.expected_public_gain: +0.001..+0.004 (central +0.002; guess from the arithmetic above; it scales with the share of a_never/swap GT nodes that have a free pool peak within 3 um, which step 0 measures)
hypotheses.expected_private_gain: Similar or larger (+0.001..+0.005): the rule uses no edge-network confidence, and private embryos are unseen by the detector like public. If a private embryo is 44b6-like (dense, under-segmented), the pool matters more (guess).
hypotheses.probability: 0.35 that it gives >= +0.002 on the public LB. For: the mechanism attacks the largest FN classes, rests on a textbook tracking component, and x138's partial version already transfers. Against: the pool may mostly hold duplicates or noise near existing nodes (the 2 um exclusion and persistence gates address this), and the added nodes can steal matches from correct nodes (measured in the lab).
hypotheses.validation_protocol: STEP 0 (today, CPU, zero GPU, ~1.5 h): download exp56's kernel output (edge_cache/*.npz with low_coords/low_score, submission.csv) for the 4 dummy clips, which are train clips with GT. For every GT node whose edge is FN under the official metric, and for all GT nodes, measure the share with a FREE pool peak (>= 0.5, > 2 um from any final node) within 3 um. KILL if < 15% of the FN-edge GT nodes have one, or if free pool peaks number > 30% of final nodes per frame (pool mostly junk). STEP 1 (lab, out of the in-sample trap as far as possible): run the exp56 kernel on 36 train videos (18 6bba stratified by density + 18 44b6, one per leak group) through a fake test dir. Keep the pre-tail checkpoint and pool, and run the tail twice per video (control / arm) in the same kernel. Official metric. SELECTION = 18 6bba to choose between the pre-registered primary and at most 2 alternates. CONFIRMATION = the 18 44b6 + 18 fresh 6bba, run once. GATE: delta >= +0.0010 overall, each embryo >= 0.0000, >= 55% of changed videos gain, node ratio change <= +2.5%, and added-node GT-hit rate in 6bba >= 0.5 x the video's annotated fraction. Why the lab is not optimistic here: the rule reads only detector peak scores and geometry, not the in-sample edge network (the channel that faked +0.016 before). The detector is in-sample on train, so annotated nuclei are already ABOVE threshold there and the train pool under-represents them. The lab bias therefore points to UNDER-estimating the gain. LB rule: adopt if the probe >= base + 0.002; tie -> keep as F2 diversification only.

hypotheses.title: Use the discarded future-context detection logits: fuse window (t-1,t) and (t,t+1) outputs for frame t (zero extra GPU)
hypotheses.mechanism: predict_video slides W=2 windows with stride 1. Frame t is detected ONLY from window (t-1,t) at position 1 (seen_frames dedup, tools/repo/scripts/predict_unet_transformer.py l.394-404), and x138 keeps this (cell 4 still gates on seen_frames). The window (t,t+1) also outputs trained detection logits for frame t (the detection loss covers every window frame, train_unet_transformer.py l.842-849), but they are thrown away. The TemporalUNet3D mixes frames through temporal attention in the deeper stages (tools/repo/src/biohub_tracking/models/temporal_unet.py l.51-75), so the two outputs for frame t see DIFFERENT context: past vs future frame. The literature is consistent that symmetric or longer temporal context helps detection and linking of nuclei. linajea uses a centred 7-frame 4D U-Net; Trackastra reports that a 2-frame window 'substantially degrades' against 6 (research/survey_linking_divisions.md #1, #3). Averaging the two logit maps is an ensemble of two genuinely different inputs, unlike flip TTA, which re-shows memorised pixels. It targets faint or entering nuclei: a_never 1,907 and part of swaps.
hypotheses.change: Patch 'tempfuse' in the x138 predict cell (cell 4 patches): keep the final fused det map (after TTA, dual-seed blend and retention guard) of the LAST frame of window (t-1,t). When window (t,t+1) is encoded, take det_t = mean(L_pos1(t-1,t), L_pos0(t,t+1)) and run _detect_cells_pooled, the V1284 refine and the lowdet dump on it. Frame 0 and the last frame keep one view. Edge prediction for the pair (t-1,t) needs the coords of t, so it moves one window later, using cached unet_out (TTA-averaged features) of window (t-1,t). This is a one-window delay; features stay the same arrays as today, so the edge net and head see no distribution shift beyond the peak positions. Calibration guard: per video, set the threshold so the number of peaks >= threshold on the fused map matches the pos-1-only count (quantile match, clamp to +-1%). The change then reorders WHICH peaks pass instead of adding nodes (avoids the node-multiplier artefact). Knob TEMPFUSE=0 -> byte-identical.

hypotheses.title: Ultrack-style hypothesis selection: low-score peaks as optional ILP nodes with a node cost
hypotheses.mechanism: Ultrack's central idea is to commit to nodes inside the ILP, choosing among segmentation hypotheses by temporal consistency, instead of thresholding first (Bragantini et al., Nat Methods 2025, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-025-02778-0). Our ILP only sees peaks >= 0.965, so a nucleus the detector scores 0.6 in every frame can never be tracked. Readmit and gapfill patch this afterwards, with local rules. tracksdata's ILPSolver, the solver the pipeline already calls, supports a per-node node_weight and overlap (mutual-exclusion) constraints (raw.githubusercontent.com/royerlab/tracksdata/main/src/tracksdata/solvers/_ilp_solver.py l.138, l.330-404). A low-score peak can therefore enter the candidate graph with a positive cost that only a consistent track can pay back. Same target classes as H1 (a_never, part of swaps). The selection uses the edge network's pair scores over the whole window rather than geometry only, which is what the literature credits for Ultrack's robustness in dense tissue.
hypotheses.change: In the x138 predict patch, append the free lowdet peaks (0.5 <= s < 0.965; already local maxima of the same map, so >= 3 um from standard peaks) to coords before candidate edges are built. Give every node attr hyp_cost = beta * (logit(0.965) - logit(s)) (0 for standard peaks) and call ILPSolver(..., node_weight=td.NodeAttr('hyp_cost'), timeout=ILP_TIMEOUT_S). The rest of the x138 chain is unchanged (relink/readmit/gapfill see the ILP node set). Knobs: HYP_MIN_SCORE 0.5, HYP_BETA in {0.5, 1, 2}; HYP=0 -> byte-identical. Check in the kernel that the installed tracksdata has node_weight (inspect.signature), else skip with a log line.

hypotheses.validation_protocol: Same 36-video lab as H1 (shared GPU run if both arms are dumped in one kernel). Report separately the gain from nodes that the relink (geometry) kept. Adopt on LB only if >= base + 0.002.

hypotheses.title: LoG/DoG blob hypotheses for z-merged nuclei (TrackMate/TGMM-style splits) feeding the H1 pool
hypotheses.mechanism: In 44b6 the a_never class is under-segmentation: two Ultrack objects ~7 um apart, blurred in z, where our detector puts one peak and the GT nucleus sits 2.3 um from the second object (research/wf_ideas_v2/r2_critic.notes.md). The peak extractor keeps only strict local maxima of the logit map in a 3x3x3 window (tools/repo/scripts/predict_unet_transformer.py l.256-295). A second nucleus that appears as a SHOULDER of its neighbour's response has no local maximum and so is not even in the lowdet pool. Classic blob detectors (TrackMate's LoG/DoG detectors; TGMM's Gaussian-mixture split test) resolve shoulders through the scale-normalised Laplacian, whose peaks separate overlapping blobs that the raw intensity cannot. Measured: our preds are farther apart than GT pairs by +0.55..+1.0 um in dense 6bba, mostly in z (neighbour-repulsion bias, r2_critic.notes.md attract3.py). Adding shoulder hypotheses to the pool lets H1's persistence gates decide.
hypotheses.change: In the x138 predict patch, after the fused det map for frame t: compute -LoG of the logit map (sigma ~ 1 grid voxel = 1.625 um isotropic, separable 3D conv on GPU), extract its local maxima (3x3x3) with logit >= logit(0.3). Keep those > 3.5 um from every standard peak and from every lowdet peak, and append them to the lowdet dump with a flag and score = sigmoid(logit). H1's extension and birth rules then treat them like other pool peaks, with an optional stricter S for flagged peaks. Knob SHOULDER=0 -> byte-identical.

In 6bba (1,740 a_never) the under-segmentation share is unmeasured. If it were 30%: 522 x 7.4e-6 = +0.0039 ceiling. Realistic after H1's gates: +0.000..+0.0015 local (guess). hypotheses.validation_protocol: Measured inside H1's lab at no extra GPU cost if the LoG maxima are dumped in the same inference run. Readout 1 (kill): share of FN-edge GT nodes with a shoulder hypothesis within 3 um and no pool peak. Kill if < 5%. Readout 2: H1 arm with vs without flagged peaks, same gate as H1 (delta >= +0.0005, each embryo >= 0, node ratio <= +1% extra). Ships only inside an H1 probe, never alone.
